ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, $ \angle ABC = 90^\circ$, $ \angle A = 60^\circ$, and $D$ is a point on side $AC$, with $ \angle DBC = 30^\circ$ and $ AC = 12\,cm$. What is the perimeter of $ \triangle ABD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ABC=90^\circ$, $\angle A=60^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle C=30^\circ$,\\
and since $\angle DBC=30^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle ABD=\angle ABC-\angle DBC=60^\circ$, and $BD=DC$,\\
thus $\angle ABD=\angle A=60^\circ$,\\
therefore $\triangle ABD$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
thus $BD=AD=AB$,\\
since $BD=DC$ and $AC=12\text{cm}$,\\
it follows that $AD=DC=\frac{1}{2}AC=6\text{cm}$,\\
thus $BD=AD=AB=6\text{cm}$,\\
therefore, the perimeter of $\triangle ABD$ is: $BD+AD+AB=6\times 3=\boxed{18\text{cm}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a triangle ABC, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is on the right side, AB is approximately vertical, BC is approximately horizontal, and AC is the oblique side from A to C. Point D is located on line segment AC, and an internal line segment BD is drawn from B to D. Then reason: It is known that ∠ABC = 90°, ∠A = 60°, so in the large triangle ABC, ∠C = 180° - 90° - 60° = 30°. Because D is on AC, ∠BCD = ∠BCA = 30°. It is also known that ∠DBC = 30°, therefore in triangle BDC, ∠DBC = ∠BCD = 30°, so the sides opposite them are equal, namely BD = DC. On the other hand, ∠ABD = ∠ABC - ∠DBC = 90° - 30° = 60°; and D is on AC, so ∠BAD = ∠BAC = 60°. Thus triangle ABD has two angles both equal to 60°, and the third angle is also 60°, so triangle ABD is an equilateral triangle, AB = BD = AD. Combining BD = DC and AD = BD, we can obtain AD = DC. Also AC = AD + DC = 12 cm, so AD = DC = 6 cm. Therefore the three sides AB, BD, AD of equilateral triangle ABD are all 6 cm, and the perimeter is 6 + 6 + 6 = 18 cm.
